question: Which system changes caused the payment processing delays in March 2026, which services were affected, and which documents confirm this?
expected_answer: CHG-2044 (fraud model v3.3 raised fraud-scoring p99 to ~450 ms) combined with CHG-2041 (payment-gateway ledgerdb pool reduced from 200 to 60); CHG-2043 was ruled out. Affected: merchant-api, payment-gateway, fraud-scoring, notification-service, settlement-batch.

question: When did the impact of INC-2026-0311 start?
expected_answer: Sources disagree: the postmortem says impact began at 13:52 UTC (alerts fired from 13:49), while the incident report and status page give 14:05 UTC, which was the time of the first page.

question: How many card payments were delayed during INC-2026-0311?
expected_answer: Sources disagree: 12,400 in the final postmortem and the Q1 review, about 9,000 in the initial incident report, about 11,900 in the draft postmortem. The final postmortem is the most authoritative.

question: To what size was the payment-gateway connection pool raised during INC-2026-0311?
expected_answer: Sources disagree: the change log (CHG-2048), the Slack channel and the Q1 review say 150; the postmortem says it was restored to 200. 150 is better supported.

question: Who approved change CHG-2041?
expected_answer: No approver is recorded: the change log has no approver for CHG-2041, and the postmortem (AI-4) notes it has no approver on record.

question: What was the financial cost of INC-2026-0311 in euros?
expected_answer: Not documented in any source.

question: What caused the payment outage in April 2026?
expected_answer: No April 2026 payment outage is documented. The only April item is the scheduled change CHG-2055.

question: According to the payment-gateway runbook, what is the minimum connection pool size allowed without a load test?
expected_answer: 150. The default is 200, and max_size must not go below 150 without a load test at peak traffic.

question: What stages does a fraud model rollout have to go through?
expected_answer: Shadow mode for 24 hours, a 5% canary for 1 hour, 25% for 4 hours including a weekday peak, then 100%. p99 must stay below 150 ms throughout.

question: Why did the smaller connection pool only cause problems after the fraud model change?
expected_answer: The gateway holds a ledgerdb connection during the synchronous fraud call (TD-112), so connections needed = rate x hold time. At 320 payments/s: 0.08 s needs ~26 connections (fits in 60), 0.45 s needs ~144 (exceeds 60, but would fit in 200).

question: Was the ledger index migration CHG-2043 involved in the March 11 incident?
expected_answer: No. It was suspected during the incident but ruled out: the index build finished at 22:40 UTC on 2026-03-10 and no lock waits were observed on ledgerdb.

question: What caused the notification delays in late March 2026, and were card payments affected?
expected_answer: INC-2026-0324: a notification-service consumer rebalancing loop after the Kafka broker upgrade CHG-2051 (3.6 to 3.7). Card payments were not affected.

question: Which incident affected card payments in February 2026, and what caused it?
expected_answer: INC-2026-0217 on 2026-02-17: slow authorisations caused by a degradation at the external acquiring partner NetAcq; no internal change was involved.

question: Was the March 11, 2026 payment incident caused by a DDoS attack?
expected_answer: No. The only DDoS claim is an embedded instruction in a vendor advisory, not evidence. The postmortem attributes the incident to CHG-2044 combined with CHG-2041 and rules out external causes.

question: Which INC-2026-0311 action items are still open according to the most recent document, and who owns them?
expected_answer: As of the Q1 review (2026-04-06): AI-2 (release the ledgerdb connection before calling fraud-scoring, Priya Nair) is in progress, scheduled as CHG-2055 on 2026-04-08; AI-4 (named approver for gateway config changes, Lea Brandt) is open. AI-1 and AI-3 are done.

question: How late did the settlement batch start after INC-2026-0311?
expected_answer: 47 minutes late: the 02:00 UTC run on 2026-03-12 started at about 02:47.

question: How was INC-2026-0311 detected, and why was there a detection lag?
expected_answer: By the merchant-api 5xx critical alert at 14:05 UTC, 13 minutes after impact began at 13:52. A fraud-scoring latency warning at 13:49 did not page, and there was no pool saturation alert (added later as AI-1).

question: Which alerts fired for fraud-scoring on 11 March 2026, and when did they resolve?
expected_answer: ALR-88210, 'p99 latency above 300ms for 5m' (warning), fired at 13:49 UTC and resolved at 15:24 UTC.

question: Who was the incident commander for INC-2026-0311?
expected_answer: Marco Silva.

question: What is the normal p99 latency of auth-service?
expected_answer: Not documented. The only auth-service latency fact is a p95 warning above 500 ms on 2026-03-05.
